sections.title: Try it in a window (a virtual machine) — the easiest start
steps: Use llmos-arm64.iso on a Mac with Apple Silicon (M1–M4) or an ARM PC, and llmos-x86_64.iso on everything else (Intel Macs and ordinary PCs). The button “Show the ISO this computer needs” points at the right one.

Mac: install the free app UTM from mac.getutm.app (open the download and drag UTM into Applications). In UTM choose Create a New Virtual Machine → Virtualize → Linux; under Boot ISO Image click Browse and pick the ISO; memory 4096 MB (6144 if the Mac has 16 GB or more), 4 CPU cores, storage 32 GB; skip the shared folder, Save, then press the big ▶ Play button.

Windows: install the free VirtualBox from virtualbox.org. Click New, name it LLM OS, choose the ISO, Type Linux, Version Other Linux (64-bit), and tick Skip Unattended Installation; give it 4096 MB memory, 4 processors and a 32 GB disk; Finish, then Start.
Linux: open the ISO in GNOME Boxes (+ → choose the ISO → Create) or virt-manager, with 4 GB memory, or run qemu-system-x86_64 -enable-kvm -m 4096 -smp 4 -cdrom llmos-x86_64.iso.
LLM OS starts in the window and runs its set-up: your language, name and time zone, then six sliders. Nothing on your computer changes; LLM OS lives only inside the window.

To keep it there between restarts, say “install LLM OS” inside the window: it installs onto the virtual machine's own disk, never onto your computer. Then remove the ISO from the virtual machine's CD drive (in its settings) so it starts from that disk.
sections.note: If the window stays black, change the virtual machine's display: in UTM pick virtio-ramfb (Display settings); in VirtualBox pick VMSVGA with 128 MB video memory. Give it at least 4 GB of memory; with less, close other programs first.

sections.title: Mac with Apple Silicon (M1, M2, M3, M4)
steps: These Macs can't start LLM OS directly yet (that needs Asahi Linux support for your Mac; it is tracked in BUILD.md). Run it in a window on this Mac instead — see Try it in a window above: the free app UTM with llmos-arm64.iso is the easiest way.

Faster option for people comfortable with Homebrew: brew install qemu llama.cpp, then press Try it in a window at the top of this page. It starts LLM OS with the language model running on the Mac's own graphics chip — several times faster at reading your requests — still entirely on this Mac.
To put LLM OS on a different computer (a PC or an Intel Mac), make a USB stick here with llmos-x86_64.iso and see PC or laptop below.
sections.note: Nothing leaves your Mac in either way: the virtual machine has no access to your files unless you share a folder, and the language model runs on this computer.

sections.title: PC or laptop (start from a USB stick, install next to Windows)
steps: Write the ISO to a USB stick with Write to a USB stick on this page (8 GB or more; the stick is erased).

If you want to keep Windows: first suspend BitLocker (Control Panel → BitLocker → Suspend protection) or write down your recovery key — turning Secure Boot off in the next step can otherwise make Windows ask for that key at the next start. Then open Disk Management, right-click the Windows partition, choose Shrink Volume and free at least 32 GB; leave it unallocated.

In the firmware (Del or F2 at the logo) turn Secure Boot off — LLM OS's boot loader is unsigned, so it will not start with Secure Boot on. Save and restart, then open the boot menu (usually F12, F11, Esc or F8) and pick the stick. UEFI and legacy/BIOS modes both work.

LLM OS starts from the stick and runs its set-up: your language, name and time zone, then six sliders (how much it asks, internet, where it thinks, model size, guidance, screen). Try it as long as you like; nothing is written to the computer yet.

To install, say “install LLM OS alongside Windows” (uses the free space you made) or “erase the whole disk and install LLM OS”. It shows a plan with the exact partitions and asks once; then it copies itself (a few minutes) and offers a restart.
After the restart a boot menu lists LLM OS and Windows. Unplug the stick.
sections.note: Minimum 4 GB RAM and 2 cores; 8 GB and 4 cores are comfortable. Wi-Fi is set up during the first run (when the sliders leave the internet on) or by saying “connect to Wi-Fi <name> with password …”.

sections.title: Intel Mac (2010 onwards)
steps: Easiest first: try it in a window with the free app UTM and llmos-x86_64.iso — see Try it in a window above.
To start it directly: write llmos-x86_64.iso to a USB stick with this page.

To dual boot: in macOS open Disk Utility, select the internal disk, click Partition, add a partition of at least 32 GB and apply; then select that new partition and click – (remove) so the space stays free (unallocated): LLM OS installs into free space, never into an existing partition. On Macs with a T2 chip, also open Startup Security Utility (hold Cmd+R at start, Utilities menu), set No Security under Secure Boot (the boot loader is unsigned), and allow booting from external media.
Plug the stick in, restart holding Option (⌥), and choose the orange EFI Boot entry.
Try LLM OS from the stick. When ready, say “install LLM OS alongside macOS”; it uses the free space you made, keeps macOS and the EFI partition, and asks once before writing.
Restart holding Option to choose between macOS and LLM OS.
sections.note: Back up your Mac (Time Machine) before changing its disk.
